questions.text: Arrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph: (P) It was a cold winter morning. (Q) She decided to brew a hot cup of tea. (R) The wind howled outside the window. (S) The warmth of the mug comforted her instantly.

options.option_text: P-R-Q-S (setting → detail → response → outcome)
R-P-S-Q (wind → morning → comfort → brewing)
Q-P-R-S (action → setting → detail → outcome)
P-Q-R-S (morning → brewing → wind → comfort)

questions.explanation: Logical flow: P sets the scene (cold morning), R adds atmospheric detail (howling wind), Q shows her response to the cold (brewing tea), S gives the outcome (warmth/comfort). P→R→Q→S is the natural cause-and-effect chain.

questions.text: Arrange: (P) Exercise also improves mental health by releasing endorphins. (Q) A sedentary lifestyle is one of the leading causes of chronic disease. (R) Regular physical activity reduces the risk of heart disease, diabetes, and obesity. (S) Despite knowing these benefits, most people fail to exercise regularly.

options.option_text: Q-R-P-S (problem → physical benefits → mental benefits → irony)
R-Q-P-S (benefits → problem → mental benefits → irony)
P-R-Q-S (mental benefits → physical → problem → irony)
Q-P-R-S (problem → mental benefits → physical → irony)

questions.explanation: Q introduces the problem (sedentary lifestyle = disease risk). R states the direct solution/benefit (exercise reduces disease). P adds another benefit (mental health/endorphins). S provides the ironic twist — despite benefits, people still don't exercise. This Q→R→P→S order follows problem → evidence → elaboration → contrast.

questions.text: Arrange: (P) The committee reviewed its findings before publishing the report. (Q) Several inconsistencies were found in the preliminary data. (R) An independent audit was commissioned to verify the results. (S) Only after the audit was the final report released to the public.

options.option_text: P-Q-R-S (review → inconsistencies → audit → publication)
Q-P-R-S (inconsistencies → review → audit → publication)
R-Q-P-S (audit → inconsistencies → review → publication)
Q-R-P-S (inconsistencies → audit → review → publication)

questions.explanation: P: committee reviews data. Q: inconsistencies found (consequence of review). R: audit commissioned (response to inconsistencies). S: final publication after audit. P→Q→R→S is strictly chronological and causal. Option B (Q before P) is tempting — inconsistencies could come first — but P ('reviewed before publishing') sets the stage for what was found.

questions.text: Arrange: (P) This made the discovery all the more remarkable. (Q) Alexander Fleming noticed an unusual mould growing on a petri dish. (R) He observed that the mould appeared to be killing the surrounding bacteria. (S) The mould had been left there by accident.

options.option_text: Q-S-R-P (observation → accident → discovery → emphasis)
Q-R-S-P (observation → killing → accident → emphasis)
S-Q-R-P (accident → observation → killing → emphasis)
R-Q-S-P (killing → observation → accident → emphasis)

questions.explanation: Q: Fleming notices the mould (initial observation). S: explains it was there by accident (background context, why it was notable). R: key discovery — mould killing bacteria. P: 'all the more remarkable' = concluding emphasis, referencing the accidental nature of the discovery. Q→S→R→P is the natural narrative arc.

questions.text: Arrange: (P) However, critics argue that technology has also deepened inequality between those with and without access. (Q) The digital revolution has transformed communication, commerce, and education worldwide. (R) Proponents point to falling costs and rising smartphone penetration as evidence of democratisation. (S) The debate reflects a broader tension between technological optimism and structural realism.

options.option_text: Q-P-R-S (claim → counter → rebuttal → synthesis)
Q-R-P-S (claim → support → counter → synthesis)
P-Q-R-S (counter → claim → support → synthesis)
R-Q-P-S (support → claim → counter → synthesis)

questions.explanation: Q makes the broad claim (digital revolution transformed the world). R supports it (proponents: costs falling, smartphones spreading). P introduces the counterargument (but critics say inequality deepened). S synthesises both sides (tension between optimism and realism). Q→R→P→S follows the standard argumentative structure: claim → support → counter → synthesis.

questions.text: Arrange: (P) These neurons form the biological basis of what psychologists call 'emotional contagion'. (Q) When we observe someone experiencing pain, mirror neurons in our brain activate as if we felt the pain ourselves. (R) This automatic neural response explains why watching someone cry often makes us feel sad too. (S) Mirror neurons were discovered in the 1990s while studying macaque monkeys.

options.option_text: S-Q-P-R (discovery → mechanism → theory name → application)
Q-P-S-R (mechanism → name → discovery → application)
S-P-Q-R (discovery → name → mechanism → application)
Q-S-P-R (mechanism → discovery → name → application)

questions.explanation: S introduces mirror neurons (historical discovery, 1990s monkeys). Q explains the mechanism (pain observation → self-activation). P names the phenomenon (emotional contagion). R gives a real-world application (watching someone cry → feeling sad). S→Q→P→R follows discovery → mechanism → concept name → example, the classic science explanation arc.

questions.text: Arrange: (P) The paradox is that language, our primary tool for self-expression, is fundamentally a shared and public system. (Q) Every act of self-expression is therefore simultaneously an act of conformity to pre-existing linguistic structures. (R) When we speak, we do not invent the words or grammar — we inherit them from our community. (S) Yet we insist that our words are uniquely and authentically our own.

options.option_text: P-R-Q-S (paradox → explanation → implication → irony)
R-P-Q-S (explanation → paradox → implication → irony)
P-R-S-Q (paradox → explanation → irony → implication)
R-Q-P-S (explanation → implication → paradox → irony)

questions.explanation: P states the central paradox (language = shared yet used for self-expression). R explains it (we inherit words/grammar, don't invent them). S introduces the tension/irony ('yet we insist our words are our own'). Q draws the philosophical implication from S (every self-expression = conformity). P→R→S→Q builds the argument: paradox → evidence → ironic observation → conclusion.

questions.stem: Arrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph about the water cycle: (P) Water evaporates from oceans and lakes when heated by the sun. (Q) This water vapour rises, cools, and condenses to form clouds. (R) Finally, the clouds release moisture as rainfall or snowfall. (S) The precipitation replenishes rivers, lakes, and underground water reserves. Which of the following is the correct sequence?

options.option_text: The correct order is P – Q – R – S
The correct order is P – Q – S – R
The correct order is Q – P – R – S
The correct order is R – S – P – Q

questions.explanation: PQRS is correct because it follows the causal chain of the water cycle: evaporation (P) produces vapour, which rises and condenses into clouds (Q); clouds release rain (R); and precipitation replenishes water bodies (S). PQSR is the most tempting distractor but is wrong because S (replenishment of rivers and lakes) cannot occur before R (the rainfall that causes it).

questions.stem: Arrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph about the invention of the printing press: (P) Gutenberg's invention of the printing press around 1440 revolutionised the spread of information. (Q) Before this invention, manuscripts were laboriously hand-copied, making books scarce and expensive. (R) The printing press made books affordable and widely accessible to ordinary people. (S) Knowledge that had once been confined to clergy and scholars now reached a far wider audience. Which of the following is the correct sequence?

options.option_text: The correct order is R – Q – P – S
The correct order is P – R – Q – S
The correct order is P – Q – R – S
The correct order is Q – P – R – S

questions.explanation: PQRS is correct: P introduces Gutenberg's invention; Q opens with 'Before this invention,' an anaphoric phrase whose referent 'this' must point to something just mentioned — namely the invention in P; R describes the immediate consequence (affordable books); and S generalises the broader cultural outcome. PRQS is wrong because inserting R between P and Q severs Q's anaphoric link ('this invention') to P, destroying coherence.

questions.stem: Arrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph about microplastics: (P) Scientists are still investigating the long-term effects of these particles on human health. (Q) Microplastics have been detected in human blood, lung tissue, and even placentas. (R) These fragments enter the food chain primarily through contaminated water and seafood. (S) When plastic waste degrades, it breaks into particles smaller than five millimetres. Which of the following is the correct sequence?

options.option_text: The correct order is S – R – Q – P
The correct order is Q – S – R – P
The correct order is P – Q – R – S
The correct order is S – Q – R – P

questions.explanation: SRQP is correct: S defines microplastics by describing how plastic degrades (definitional opening); R explains the pathway by which these fragments enter the food chain; Q presents the alarming consequence (detection in human organs); P closes with the open scientific question. SQRP is the strongest distractor but is wrong because it places Q (presence in human tissues) before R (the food-chain entry route), showing the effect before explaining the mechanism.

questions.stem: Arrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph about the Bretton Woods system: (P) The Bretton Woods Conference of 1944 established the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank. (Q) These institutions were designed to prevent the economic instability that had contributed to the Second World War. (R) Member countries agreed to peg their currencies to the US dollar, which was itself convertible to gold. (S) This fixed-exchange system eventually collapsed in 1971 when the United States suspended dollar-gold convertibility. Which of the following is the correct sequence?

options.option_text: The correct order is P – R – Q – S
The correct order is Q – P – R – S
The correct order is P – Q – S – R
The correct order is P – Q – R – S

questions.explanation: PQRS is correct: P introduces the conference and its institutions; Q's opening phrase 'These institutions' is a direct anaphoric reference to the IMF and World Bank named in P, so Q must follow immediately; R describes the operative mechanism (the dollar-gold peg); and S narrates the system's collapse — the logical endpoint. PRQS is wrong because inserting R between P and Q breaks Q's anaphora ('These institutions') by separating it from its referent.

questions.stem: Arrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph about school libraries and reading: (P) Children who read extensively show measurably stronger vocabulary and analytical reasoning skills. (Q) Schools that reduce library funding consistently record a decline in student reading proficiency scores. (R) Yet many policymakers continue to treat school libraries as expendable budget items. (S) Research consistently links reading habits formed during childhood to long-term academic achievement. Which of the following is the correct sequence?

options.option_text: The correct order is S – P – Q – R
The correct order is P – S – R – Q
The correct order is S – P – R – Q
The correct order is R – S – P – Q

questions.explanation: SPRQ is correct: S opens with the general research consensus; P provides a specific supporting finding; R introduces a contradiction via the adversative 'Yet,' which must follow a positive claim (P) to create effective contrast; Q closes with empirical evidence of the damage caused by the policy in R. SPQR is wrong because Q (decline in proficiency due to library cuts) is a direct consequence of R (treating libraries as expendable) — effect cannot precede cause.

questions.stem: Arrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph about deliberative democracy: (P) The assumption that rational deliberation alone can settle political disputes ignores the role of incommensurable moral frameworks. (Q) Where fundamental values diverge irreconcilably, logical argument may fail to produce consensus even among well-intentioned citizens. (R) Deliberative democracy theory holds that citizens, through reasoned dialogue, can collectively arrive at just political outcomes. (S) This does not render politics a mere contest of power, but demands that persuasion engage deeply with emotion and shared identity. Which of the following is the correct sequence?

options.option_text: The correct order is P – R – Q – S
The correct order is R – P – S – Q
The correct order is R – Q – P – S
The correct order is R – P – Q – S

questions.explanation: RPQS is correct: R states the theory to be examined; P challenges its core assumption (the word 'assumption' presupposes a prior claim — the theory in R); Q deepens the critique by specifying the condition under which rational argument collapses; S ends with a nuanced qualification that redeems the argument from cynicism. RPSQ is the strongest distractor but is wrong because S ('This does not render politics a mere contest of power...') qualifies the failure-of-logic point established in Q — S placed before Q would qualify a point not yet made.

questions.stem: Arrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph about regulatory capture: (P) The phenomenon of regulatory capture occurs when oversight agencies begin prioritising the interests of the very industries they are mandated to regulate. (Q) Scholars attribute this drift to lobbying pressure, information asymmetry, and shared professional networks between regulators and industry executives. (R) The problem intensifies significantly when regulators anticipate lucrative private-sector careers after completing their public service tenure. (S) Ultimately, capture erodes democratic accountability as policy decisions come to reflect industry preferences over the public interest. Which of the following is the correct sequence?

options.option_text: The correct order is P – R – Q – S
The correct order is P – Q – R – S
The correct order is Q – P – R – S
The correct order is P – Q – S – R

questions.explanation: PQRS is correct: P defines regulatory capture; Q's phrase 'this drift' is an anaphoric echo of the agencies drifting toward industry described in P, making Q the immediate follow-up that surveys causes; R then narrows to one specific intensifying mechanism (the revolving-door incentive); S delivers the systemic democratic consequence as the conclusion. PRQS is a strong distractor because R may seem to follow P naturally, but Q's anaphora 'this drift' specifically ties it to P — Q must precede R, not follow it.
